what: The only two events the live corpus solves, and what origin/main's unweighted solver returns for them. Captured from the hear-tdoa CronJob's own output so the referent is the configuration that actually runs, not a synthetic array.

provenance.pool: hear pool snapshot 2026-09-11: 7,758 node rows, 9,356 phone rows
provenance.margin_note: ⚠️8.608 ms, DERIVED from this array's own pair bounds at margin_frac 0.25. NOT associate.MARGIN_S, which is 0.030 s = 87.1% of the tightest pair bound. The CronJob runs the derived one; measuring at the library default measures a configuration nothing runs.
provenance.survey: survey.json nodes 1/2/3 (nyquist, mach, rankine); node 4 puc is refused

how_to_read.solution_origin_main: THE BIT-FOR-BIT REFERENT. Produced by running origin/main's hear/solve/point.py, in this repo's test environment, on the arrivals below. An unweighted call, or a call whose sigmas are all equal, must reproduce every one of these floats exactly.
how_to_read.solution_cronjob: What the CronJob itself published, kept as provenance and NOT as a bit referent. ⚠️event 1's north_m differs from solution_origin_main by one ulp (-0.10293995289100526 vs -0.10293995289100531) although point.py and placement.py were both already at this commit when that run executed. The difference is the machine, not the code: a least_squares fit is reproducible within an environment and not across BLAS builds. Any 'bit-identical' claim about this solver is a within-environment claim, and a test that pinned these numbers would fail on the cluster for a reason that is not a regression.
how_to_read.non_finite: A non-finite float is stored as the STRING "inf"/"-inf"/"nan" -- hdop/vdop/pdop are inf at three receivers. Bare Infinity is what json.dump writes and it is not valid JSON (RFC 8259), so anything but Python choked on this file.
how_to_read.event_keys_move: ⚠️event_key is a content address of the member pool_keys, so it changes when association picks a different member set for the same physical event. Re-running hear_tdoa on a later pool snapshot reproduced baa6c4c3 unchanged but returned 988e7625 where this file records 9108b0ac -- same t0 to 10 ms, different member set. That is pool drift, not a solver change: origin/main's driver and the weighted one both emit 988e7625 on the same corpus copy. Do not chase a missing key here; the ARRIVALS are what this fixture is for.

solution_cronjob.note: source height was DECLARED as 0.00 m, not measured: two unknowns, so three nodes suffice. Every reported coordinate is conditional on that height being right -- if the source is 10 m up and this said 0, the horizontal answer absorbs the error.
